commit_message:
[Merged] Bug 1867249, part 1: Implemented new cache to determine selected nodes. r=sefeng,dom-core

Determining if a node is selected is a super-hot code path,
which at times introduces jank both in Reflow and Painting.
This is due to each node comparing its position to the range's start and end point,
which even happens several times (`nsINode::IsSelected()` and `Selection::LookupSelection()`).
In worst cases, this can lead to reflow which takes several minutes.

This patch introduces a cache which contains all fully selected nodes,
and lives throughout one `PresShell::DoReflow()` call.
Collecting all selected nodes of a selection is very fast.
The selected nodes are then stored in a hash set.
During reflow the check if a node is selected first checks the cache
if the node is fully selected, and otherwise goes through the existing
code to check if the node is partially selected.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D217794

fix_commit_message:
Bug 1943179 - Add `[[nodiscard]]` to `ContentIterator` methods that return `nsresult`. r=masayuki

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D235361
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 6624852dc946 on top of intro 70014fe558dd via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (UninitializedMemory): The `UnsafePreContentIterator::Init()` method returns an `nsresult` that can indicate failure (e.g., if the range is invalid or collapsed). When the return value is not checked, a failed initialization leaves the iterator's internal pointers (`mCurNode`, `mFirst`, `mLast`, `mClosestCommonInclusiveAncestor`) uninitialized. Subsequently calling `iter.IsDone()` and `iter.Next()` on this uninitialized iterator will dereference garbage or poison pointer values, leading to crashes or potential use-after-free conditions. Root cause: The root cause is twofold: (1) The `ContentIteratorBase` class did not default-initialize its internal pointer members (`mCurNode`, `mFirst`, `mLast`, `mClosestCommonInclusiveAncestor`), leaving them with indeterminate values when `Init()` fails. (2) The calling code in `SelectionNodeCache::MaybeCollect()` did not check the return value of `iter.Init(range)` before using the iterator, allowing the code to proceed with an improperly initialized iterator.
